items.title: Implement a Queue
items.description:
In this lab, you will implement a queue data structure using functions. A queue is a First-In-First-Out (FIFO) data structure where elements are added to the back of the queue and removed from the front.

**Objective:** Fulfill the user stories below and get all the tests to pass to complete the lab.

**User Stories:**

1. You should have an `initQueue` function that returns an object with a `collection` property set to an empty array.
1. You should have an `enqueue` function that adds an element to the back of the queue.
1. You should have a `dequeue` function that removes and returns the front element of the queue, or `undefined` if there isn't one.
1. You should have a `front` function that returns the front element of the queue without removing it, or `undefined` if there isn't one.
1. You should have a `size` function that returns the number of elements in the queue.
1. You should have an `isEmpty` function that returns `true` if the queue is empty and `false` otherwise.

**Note:** The tests for `dequeue`, `front`, `size`, and `isEmpty` use the `enqueue` function to add elements to the queue, so it is best to implement `enqueue` first. The final test checks that all of your functions work together.

hints.text: The `enqueue` function should add an element to the back of the queue.
The `dequeue` function should remove and return the front element of the queue.
`dequeue` should return `undefined` when called on an empty queue.
`enqueue` should continue to add elements to the back of the queue after elements are removed from the front.
Different queue instances should not share state.
The `front` function should return the front element of the queue without removing it.
The `front` function should return `undefined` when called on an empty queue.
The `size` function should return the correct number of elements in the queue.
The `isEmpty` function should return `true` for an empty queue.
The `isEmpty` function should return `false` for a non-empty queue.
The `isEmpty` function should return `true` after all elements are removed from the queue.
All of your queue functions should work together.
